title: The Iron Atlas
premise: In the occupied port city of Vellamare, Sable Oyelaran, an apprentice clockmaker of mixed heritage, is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock and discovers hidden inside it a ledger documenting a massacre the victors' regime has officially erased. When a census taker's probing questions reveal that Sable's own family name appears in the ledger, staying invisible becomes impossible, and they must choose between silence and testimony. Racing against the regime's historians who are about to seal the official record, Sable allies with a disgraced archivist, Ilse Marchetti, with whom they fall in love despite the danger duty forbids. The story ends with Sable testifying before an international commission as the master clock strikes, the truth entered into record at cost of their workshop, their anonymity, and nearly their life.
about_author: August Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging suppressed municipal records in postwar Europe. They write historical fiction about ordinary people who keep accounts the powerful would prefer lost.

chapters.title: The Silence Between Gears
chapters.summary: Sable Oyelaran, POV. Summoned to the observatory to repair the master clock, Sable navigates the occupied city's checkpoints and unspoken rules, establishing how fifteen years of calculated invisibility work. The emotional beat is wary competence: Sable knows every silence that keeps people safe, and resents needing them.

chapters.title: A Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Census taker Bram Holt interviews Sable for the new registry, asking about family origins with unusual precision. His questions echo words Sable half-remembers from childhood. The beat is dread dawning slowly: someone is looking for Oyelarans specifically, and the census may be a net, not paperwork.

chapters.title: What the Clock Kept
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Repairing the clock's escapement, Sable finds a hidden compartment containing a hand-kept ledger: names, dates, and testimony from the Harbor District massacre fifteen years ago, including the signature of an Oyelaran. The beat is vertigo—the past Sable buried is documented, waiting.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Debt
chapters.summary: Ilse Marchetti, POV. A disgraced former state archivist recognizes the ledger's provenance when Sable cautiously seeks authentication. Ilse explains the victors' historians will seal the official record within weeks, after which all counter-evidence becomes legally meaningless. The beat is reluctant alliance between two people who trust no one.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable and Ilse, POV. They verify the ledger against surviving fragments, discovering the massacre was ordered to seize shipping contracts—and that Sable's father was the clerk who hid this copy before disappearing. The beat is grief transformed into purpose; Sable stops running from the name Oyelaran.

chapters.title: The Historian's Banquet
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. Infiltrating a victory-anniversary reception, Ilse confirms the sealing date and identifies Commissioner Vasseur, the historian personally erasing the Harbor District. She narrowly escapes detection with help from an unexpected ally: census taker Bram, whose questions were conscience, not surveillance. The beat is hope complicated by risk.

chapters.title: Love Against the Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. As the deadline closes in, Sable and Ilse admit what duty forbids them to feel; a quiet night in the workshop becomes a vow to survive each other. But Vasseur's agents trace the ledger's repair order back to the observatory. The beat is tenderness shadowed by the knowledge that love makes them both targetable.

chapters.title: The Raid on Rue Cendre
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Regime agents raze Sable's workshop seeking the ledger; Sable escapes through the clockmaker's tunnels with the book strapped to their chest while Ilse is taken. The beat is terror and fury—everything invisible Sable built burns, and only the truth remains worth carrying.

chapters.title: Thirteen Minutes to Midnight
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable and Ilse, POV. Climax. Sable trades the ledger's location to reach the international commission hearing as Ilse, interrogated by Vasseur, stalls with misfiled records. Sable takes the stand as the master clock—repaired by their own hands—strikes midnight, entering testimony into the record seconds before the seal descends. The beat is triumph purchased with exposure.

chapters.title: The Long Minute After
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Resolution. The commission suspends the seal; Vasseur falls from favor; Ilse is released, and she and Sable begin rebuilding—not invisibility, but a public archive in the burned workshop's place. The final beat is quiet resolve: justice outside the law was necessary once; now the law must answer to the record.
